sections.overview: The greater prairie-chicken is a North American grouse of open grasslands.
sections.identification: Males gather at open display grounds, where their courtship includes booming calls and conspicuous movements.
sections.habitat: It uses tall- and mixed-grass prairie, with different grass heights and cover needed for nesting, feeding and display.
sections.diet: Adults eat mainly plant material, while young chicks rely heavily on insects.
sections.behavior: Males display communally at leks, where females visit to choose mates.
sections.reproduction: Nesting cover is important near display grounds, and chicks leave the nest soon after hatching.
sections.ecology: It is one of three living species in Tympanuchus, alongside the lesser prairie-chicken and sharp-tailed grouse.
sections.conservation: Conversion and fragmentation of prairie have reduced populations; the Attwater’s prairie-chicken is a particularly imperiled subspecies.
